items.root_cause_found: Partially, and the answer is not the one the work order proposed. The order's hypothesis was a template-coverage gap (manifest has cell templates for MEAT/WOOD/COAL/IRON only, so an anchored 冰原巨兽 cell cannot be identified). That fits the symptom but not the cause. On the production frame that failed, selected_tab_left() returned left_px=2.0 while the white bracket actually sits on the third visible cell at x=282.5: nine strokes produced FOUR stroke pairs in the accepted 130..175 px window, and the code took the first. So the anchor was 280 px wrong and the template mismatch that followed (33.75 / 34.63 / 35.98 / 36.48 against a 6.0 gate) was a consequence of cropping from the wrong place, not evidence of missing templates. Had the mis-anchored cell happened to match a template, a wrong offset would have been accepted and the executor handed a wrong tap target -- precisely the failure the strip geometry exists to prevent. Fixing that (choose the anchor by evidence, not by stroke order) does resolve the archived frame. But it does NOT resolve the live frames, and the reason is a second, independent defect: the strip geometry model does not match the live panel. Measured on the live frame (23:37:27Z): the bracket is on the second visible cell at anchor x=172 (pair 172->317, gap 145, correctly detected), which yields offset ~399 -- consistent with the 400 independently recorded for the same panel position in the archived 2026-09-14 evidence -- yet that offset predicts MEAT's cell at x=487 while MEAT actually sits at roughly x=430. The calibrated pitch is 157 px while the live strip advances ~145-150 px, so the prediction drifts by about a third of a cell over three tabs and no reviewed template accepts it.

items.blocker: The acceptance requires at least 2 live verifier PASS on SELECT_RESOURCE with MAA capture and MAA action evidence. Both live attempts failed with executed=false because the target resolver still returns None, and it returns None for a reason this work order does not cover: the calibrated strip geometry (pitch 157 px, first_left -0.5333) does not match the live panel (cells advance ~145-150 px), and it was calibrated on 2026-09-14 frames. Fixing the anchor selection removed one whole class of wrong offsets, but the predicted positions of the four gatherable tabs still land outside the template gates on live frames. The two defects are independent, and only the first is in this order's scope; the second is a recalibration that needs several live frames captured at known selected tabs, which is a separate measurement job.
items.recommended_codex_review: Three decisions. (1) Is strip recalibration the right next order, and should it use the already-archived dataset/truth_audit/resource_cells_20260914_120027/ select-each frames (MEAT/WOOD/COAL/IRON at known selections) as its calibration set, capturing fresh frames only where the live panel differs from 2026-09-14? That is the smallest path to a real offset. (2) Note that the anchor-order bug is fixed and worth keeping regardless of the recalibration, because it removed a path that could hand the executor a wrong tap target whenever a spurious stroke pair preceded the real bracket -- that class of failure is not visible in aggregate success rates until it causes a wrong-tab selection. (3) The order's own hypothesis was wrong in a way worth recording: it read the symptom (templates do not cover three tabs) as the cause, when measurement showed the crops were being taken from the wrong place. If the next order is written from this result, it should not assume template coverage is the limiter.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-16T04:15Z. The blocker's own diagnosis is REFUTED: the strip pitch was never wrong (measured 157/158 px on frames with a known selection, matching the configured 157). The defect was the template ceiling, 6.0, sitting BELOW the largest value its own calibration frames produce (correct population 0.00..6.49 vs wrong 10.65..25.09), plus a second defect found after it: the client draws no bracket until a tab is selected, so a freshly opened panel had no anchor at all and the offset stayed None. Both fixed; SELECT_RESOURCE now succeeds live and the gather chain completes end to end.
